messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: `DB_CONN_QUEUE_HIGH` fired for service `db-connections-high` (severity: P2). Alert: pgbouncer client queue length > 95% for > 3m. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/example/d/pgbouncer-queues

maria-oncall: Acked. I'm jumping in. Seeing 5xx spike from 0.1% -> ~1.3% in the last 5m. Latency tail for read requests up from 120ms -> 600ms. Sending initial checks to runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/db-conn-pressure

kevin-sre: On the DB side now. `ssh ops@pg-host` -> inside pgbouncer, `SHOW POOLS;` output noisy: several pools at `cl_active=900 cl_waiting=380` and `max_client_conn=1000`. Some idle connections stuck. Looks like client traffic burst plus a slow query pattern.

kevin-sre: ```
# pgbouncer SHOW POOLS snapshot
database  user    cl_active  cl_waiting  sv_active  sv_idle  maxwait
app_db    app     912        387         120        8        0.95
payments  worker  120        60          20         1        0.78
```

alex-eng: Maria/Kevin — do we have an immediate mitigation? Options: scale pgbouncer, kill long-idle sessions, or shed background traffic. We should prefer quick, reversible actions. Recommend: 1) scale poolers 2) throttle non-essential background workers 3) clear idle backends.

maria-oncall: Kicking off scaling and quick throttles. Scaling pg-bouncer deployment now: `kubectl scale deploy pg-bouncer --replicas=6 -n infra-db` (was 3). Also toggling feature-flag to throttle ingestion workers (non-critical). Patch command: `kubectl patch cm ff-config -n prod -p '{"data":{"throttle-ingest":"true"}}'`

maria-oncall: Patch applied, feature flag broadcasted. Deploy affecting ~2% of traffic (background ingest).

kevin-sre: Scaling confirmed. `kubectl get pods -l app=pg-bouncer -n infra-db` shows 6 ready in ~45s. Re-run `SHOW POOLS` -> cl_waiting down from ~380 -> ~70. Latency median improving.

kevin-sre: Also found ~40 idle sessions older than 90m from batch workers. Running cleanup: ```SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='idle' AND backend_start < now() - interval '90 minutes' AND application_name ILIKE 'batch-%';``` Will monitor for any side-effects.

sara-support: Heads up — Support is seeing error reports for the payments flow in EU region. Estimated impacted customers: 24 accounts, increased checkout failures ~7/min. I've posted a privacy-safe note to the status page and alerted Sales. Link: https://status.redwood/incidents/1778889999

maria-oncall: Thanks Sara. Adding customer impact to the incident log. Noting affected flows: payments.checkout, billing.scheduled-invoice. No PII exposed; failures are 500/DB_CONN errors.

kevin-sre: After scaling + terminates, queue length stabilized around 25-50, 5xx rate dropping back to ~0.2%. Continued monitoring for 15m. No rolling restarts required.

redis-bot: Warning: redis cache miss rate for payments increased 3x following throttling (expected transient). Cache hit %: 64 -> 42. See: https://grafana.redwood/d/redis/payments-hits

alex-eng: Good catch. That spike in cache misses explains some of the increased load; we'll keep cache warming and TTLs in mind for remediation. If we see reoccurrence, add dedicated cache pool for payments.

maria-oncall: Current action summary: scaled pgbouncer 3->6, applied FF throttle to ingestion, terminated stale idle DB sessions, notified Support & Sales, status page update live. Monitoring metrics: queue length, 5xx rate, p99 latency.

tom-oncall: I can take a monitored handoff in 25m and run the 2-hour watch. Will keep an eye on the payments customers and the cache metric. If things look stable, we'll close the PD alert and mark as mitigated.

kevin-sre: Agree. I'll stay on for another 30m to catch any DB-side regressions and prepare a follow-up PR to tweak `max_client_conn` and connection-timeout defaults for pgbouncer.

maria-oncall: Handing off to Tom for the steady-state watch. Documenting next steps: create a post-incident ticket to investigate root cause (likely background job surge + cache miss amplification), propose: increase pgbouncer headroom, improve connection pooling from app, add circuit-breaker for payment retries, and a controlled warmup for caches after throttles.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: `DB_CONN_QUEUE_HIGH` acknowledged by maria-oncall.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident auto-resolve check in 30m unless alert re-fires.

sara-support: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups for the 24 impacted customers and prepare a CX note with ETA and mitigation summary.

tom-oncall: taking handoff — watching for next 2 hours. If 5xx goes above 0.5% or queue length > 120 again, I'll re-open and escalate to on-call lead.

maria-oncall: Thanks team. Closing my immediate actions. Leaving detailed steps in the runbook comment. :thumbsup:
